prompt: The robot fills two pockets. What appears on the screen, in order?

options.text: `2` then `9`. pocket holds 2 and spare holds 9; print reads each pocket.
options.feedback: Right. Each assignment stored a number in its own name, and each print reads the pocket it is given.

options.text: `9` then `9`. print shows the last number written anywhere.
options.feedback: print(pocket) reads the pocket named pocket, not the program's last number. pocket holds 2.

options.text: `pocket` then `spare`. print writes the name instead of reading the pocket.
options.feedback: An unquoted name tells print which pocket to read. The screen gets the numbers 2 and 9.

options.text: `2` then `9`. Names keep their first number, so each print shows it.
options.feedback: Add pocket = 6 before the prints: the screen shows 6 then 9 — a new assignment replaces the pocket's number.
options.partial_reason: Right: 2, then 9. Wrong: that names keep their first number; a new assignment replaces it.

explanation: pocket = 2 stores 2 and spare = 9 stores 9. print(pocket) reads 2 and print(spare) reads 9: two lines, in order.
